newsitem.title: UK: Barings bondholders expect court hearing in July.
newsitem.headline: Barings bondholders expect court hearing in July.

text.p: An action group representing holders of a 100 million pounds of loan notes issued by collapsed British investment bank Barings said it expects a court hearing in July to approve a scheme whereby they and other bondholders and preference shareholders will receive some compensation.

But Jonathan Stone, chairman of the Barings 9-1/4 percent Perpetual Noteholders Action Group (BPNAG), told Reuters that he was not very pleased with the amount of compensation the bondholders will get.
"I am very pleased that things are coming to an end but I cannot say I'm very pleased with the quantum (of compensation)," Stone said.

He said ther would be a hearing in the High Court, probably in July, when "all the ducks have to be in a row", refering to loose ends which still have to be tidied up before a scheme of arrangement can be put to vice-chancellor Sir Richard Scott.
Sources closed to the deal refused to discuss the amount of compensation but a figure of 25 percent has been mentioned in recent press reports.
The deal also covers a total of $300 million of bonds issued in 1986 and 1994.
Barings collapsed in February 1995, under the weight of losses amounting to 800 million pounds casued by unauthorised derivatives trading executed by rogue trader Nick Leeson in Singapore.
The bank was taken over by Internationale Nederlanden Groep and now trades as ING Barings.
ING is thought to be a party to the deal as are securities house Hoare Govett, now owned by ABN AMRO, BZW, the investment banking arm of Barclays, and Cazenove and Co.
